bounded_leaf.tested_scope: Deterministic role-local synthetic two-contender state machine derived only from prior own STATE and frozen sanitized controls. The transition relation was append-only migration binding -> append-only claim -> idempotent effect commit. Cases covered stale reads, simultaneous same-binding contenders, an altered-binding loser, and an ABA-like replacement attempt. No public sources, other-role/O/downstream semantics, repository chronology beyond own STATE, real external effects, scheduler mutation, wait/retry, or second leaf were used.

transition_rules.migration_binding: create-once CAS from absent to one legacy->new binding; existing identical binding is observed idempotently, existing different binding rejects the contender; no delete or replace transition is admitted
transition_rules.claim: create-once CAS from absent to new_fingerprint+payload hash; existing same-key/same-payload is idempotent, existing same-key/different-payload rejects
transition_rules.effect_commit: first matching claimed key/payload changes committed=false to committed=true; later same-key/same-payload commits are no-ops; conflicting payload is rejected before effect mutation
transition_rules.aba_guard: because migration and claim records are append-only in the accepted transition relation, an observed existing record can never legally cycle through replacement/deletion back to the same visible value; a replace attempt is rejected even when it names the current record as expected-old

steps: C1 and C2 both read migration absent
C1 migration CAS(absent->canonical) succeeds
C2 stale migration CAS(absent->canonical) fails then observes identical canonical binding
C1 and C2 both read claim absent
C2 claim CAS(absent->key+payload_v1) succeeds
C1 stale claim CAS fails then observes identical key+payload_v1 claim
C1 commits effect once; C2 same-key/same-payload commit is idempotent no-op
same-key/payload_v2 conflict probe rejects
both contenders propose the identical canonical migration binding from absent
C1 wins migration CAS; C2 loses expected-absent CAS and validates the identical durable binding
C2 wins claim CAS; C1 loses and validates the identical key+payload_v1 claim
C2 commits effect; C1 replay is idempotent no-op
same-key/payload_v2 conflict probe rejects
C1 migration CAS(absent->canonical) succeeds
C2 stale expected-absent CAS for legacy->altered_new fails
C2 observes canonical binding mismatch and is rejected before claim
C1 claims payload_v1 and commits effect once
same-key/payload_v2 conflict probe rejects
C1 creates canonical migration binding
C2 observes canonical record and attempts canonical->altered replacement using the current canonical record as expected-old
append-only transition guard rejects replacement before migration state mutation
no delete/reinsert transition exists, so visible canonical value cannot complete an ABA cycle
canonical claim and effect commit proceed once
same-key/payload_v2 conflict probe rejects

bounded_leaf.validated_property: Within this exact synthetic two-contender scope, create-once CAS for the migration binding and claim, identical-record idempotent observation, same-key/different-payload rejection, and an append-only no-replacement transition relation yield exactly one durable migration binding and at most one committed effect across all tested stale-read, same-binding, altered-binding and ABA-like schedules.
